Greedy decoding repeatedly chooses the highest conditional probability and can enter self-reinforcing loops under the model's learned distribution. Low temperature sharpens that preference. Repetition penalties reduce scores of previously used tokens; min-p sampling retains tokens whose probability exceeds a fraction of the current maximum. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192)

$$A=\{i:p_i\ge p_{min}\max_jp_j\}.$$

Neither guarantees no repetition or factuality. Penalizing repeated tokens can damage names, code, or legitimate repeated phrases; min-p may retain only the dominant loop token if the distribution is very peaked. Evaluate task-specific decoding and consider model/data issues rather than treating a sampling knob as a universal cure.
